name: Dialog (Modal)
description: A window overlaid on the primary window that traps focus and prevents user interaction with content outside the active dialog until it is closed.

raweb_criteria.reason: The dialog's role and accessible name must be exposed to assistive technologies.
Open, close and every control inside must work with keyboard and any pointing device.
Opening a modal is a change of context: it must be user-initiated, never automatic on load or on focus.
Focus must stay visible on every control inside the dialog, including against the backdrop.
Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to the invoking element on close, keeping the navigation sequence coherent.
The Tab loop is only compliant because Escape and a visible close button let the keyboard user leave. A loop with no keyboard exit is a keyboard trap.

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves focus to next tabbable element inside the dialog; wraps from last to first
Moves focus to previous tabbable element inside the dialog; wraps from first to last

roles.description: Identifies the element as a dialog. Implicit on `<dialog>` — do not add it manually.

required_attributes.description: Set to 'dialog'. Implicit on the native `<dialog>` element — only needed when building from a `<div>`.
Marks content outside the dialog as inert to assistive technologies. Set automatically by showModal() — only needed when building from a `<div>`.
Accessible name, preferably aria-labelledby referencing the visible dialog title.

optional_attributes.description: References descriptive content within the dialog, announced after the name.
State reflecting whether the dialog is rendered. Read it, never set it: the open attribute opens a NON-modal dialog with no focus trap, no top layer and no inert background.

notes: Prefer the native `<dialog>` element with .showModal(): the browser provides the focus trap, Escape handling, background inertness, top layer stacking and focus restoration for free.
Never open a `<dialog>` by setting the open attribute or property — that produces a non-modal dialog. Only .showModal() creates modal semantics.
Focus must be trapped inside the dialog — Tab/Shift+Tab must not escape
On open, set focus to the first focusable element or a static element for long content
On close, return focus to the element that invoked the dialog
Content outside the dialog should be inert (use the inert attribute or aria-hidden='true')
Never put aria-hidden='true' on a container that still holds focusable elements — use inert instead, which removes both semantics and focusability
For destructive actions, focus the least destructive action button
